name: Radical Centrism
summary: Radical centrism is a pragmatic reform outlook that claims to be radical about institutional change and centrist about method, borrowing market tools from the right and social goals from the left. Its adherents favor regulated markets, fiscal responsibility, school choice, universal coverage built on private insurance, need-based rather than race-based preferences, and electoral reforms that loosen two-party dominance. It accepts capitalism and representative democracy and describes itself as idealism without illusions.
scope: The 2000s North American strand set out by Ted Halstead and Michael Lind (The Radical Center, 2001, New America) and Mark Satin (Radical Middle, 2004 and radicalmiddle.com), as summarized by Wikipedia. It excludes the Third Way of Blair and Giddens, which many radical centrists reject, and personal politics of individual figures such as Lind's restrictionism or leaders like Macron. Many issues are unaddressed by these texts, so those answers are low-confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Satin's manifesto backs universal coverage built on private insurance, and Halstead and Lind propose a mandatory Swiss-style insurance system, so the state guarantees coverage without running it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The sources propose wage subsidies and guaranteed work rather than a higher wage floor, and nothing says radical centrists favor or oppose a substantial rise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Radical centrists favor market-based solutions to social problems but under public-interest regulation, so they lean toward markets without the flat claim that markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: The manifesto accepts corporate capitalism and dismisses socialist economics as a relic, and the reform proposals work through choice and regulation rather than nationalization.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Halstead and Lind pair a progressive consumption tax and restored inheritance tax with abolishing the corporate income tax, which gives no clear verdict on substantially higher taxes on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: The review notes Halstead and Lind are silent on labor and treat unions as just another special interest, so the position is neither pro nor anti. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nothing in the sources elevates property rights above public needs; a pragmatic reformer who accepts regulation would not treat property as nearly inviolable, though this is inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Radical centrists want markets carefully regulated to serve the public good, and the manifesto seeks laws and regulations that make corporations better employers.

cut-welfare.rationale: The manifesto calls for generous assistance conditioned on work and training and means-tested safety nets, which reforms welfare rather than cutting it as dependency-creating.

worker-ownership.rationale: The manifesto accepts corporate capitalism; worker ownership is not proposed, though individual development accounts spread asset ownership. Inferred from the acceptance of corporate capitalism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The sources pair vigilant security against terrorism with attention to its roots but say nothing on surveillance, so adherents are plausibly split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: None of the sources address drug policy, and radical centrists range from libertarian-leaning to cautious, so no direction can be inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the focus on civility and dialogue does not settle whether law should restrict speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Radical centrists stress reforming institutions and building a new majority through democratic politics, and they criticize triangulating leaders; bypassing gridlock by a strong leader is not part of that. Inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: The manifesto and Wikipedia describe radical centrists as wanting reformed, effective government, not its abolition; they explicitly do not seek to overthrow representative democracy.

limit-guns.rationale: Guns are not addressed in the sources, and radical centrists mix left and right positions.

empower-police-military.rationale: The manifesto wants a strong supple military, but it also criticizes getting tough on crime as a neoliberal reflex, so broad police and military expansion is not clearly endorsed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No source addresses sex work, so no direction can be inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The manifesto rejects one-size-fits-all programs and empowers individual schools, yet Satin's strand says national leadership matters and local activism alone is not enough.

rehabilitation.rationale: Problem-solving courts and mediation in the manifesto suggest a rehabilitative, practical approach to justice, though prisons are not discussed directly.

traditional-family.rationale: The sources do not address family structure, and radical centrists mix personal-responsibility themes with a keep-the-gains view of counter-culture changes.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The manifesto lists gay rights among counter-culture gains to keep, but marriage specifically is not discussed, so this is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion is not addressed in the sources and radical centrists are not unified on it.

more-religion-public.rationale: The manifesto cites religious tolerance and shared faith values but proposes no policy role for religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Radical centrists replace race-based affirmative action with need-based aid and favor race-neutral ideals, while still valuing racial healing, so they back remedy but not racial preferences.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no basis for a direction.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed; the manifesto criticizes the balkanization of racial groups, but cultural preservation is not a stated theme.

gradual-change.rationale: The statement joins two ideas the movement treats differently: radical centrists call tinkering insufficient and want substantial reform, but they pursue it through elections and existing institutions (s1, s2). The halves cancel out, so 0 at low confidence.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not addressed in the manifesto or the review; Lind personally favored restriction while other strands differ, so the strand is split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wikipedia lists participation in global governance among radical centrist positions, though the sources give little detail.

free-trade.rationale: The manifesto supports free trade with a conscience that helps developing-world workers, so adherents favor trade but with conditions that stop short of the statement's strong claim.

nation-first.rationale: Radical centrists support global governance and developing-world assistance, so putting national interest above cooperation is not their stance; this is inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The manifesto explicitly supports humanitarian armed intervention to prevent genocide and mass atrocities.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are not addressed; the radical centrist emphasis on realism without illusions makes open borders an unlikely goal. Inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Radical centrists see an Information Age with large untapped opportunities and favor shared growth, so limiting growth is unlikely; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The manifesto promotes diversified energy paths including conservation and renewables but does not call for drastic government action on climate, so the answer is split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The manifesto is cautiously optimistic about biotechnology and Wikipedia stresses new Information Age opportunities, though neither claims technology solves most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The manifesto lists nuclear among seven energy paths to support as they become ready, which implies support for it alongside others.

revolution-justified.rationale: The manifesto says the radical middle does not seek to overthrow corporate capitalism or representative democracy, and reform proceeds through institutional change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Radical centrism emphasizes pragmatism and technocratic problem solving but also democratic reform and building a majority, so the sources do not favor either side.

central-planning.rationale: The manifesto rejects socialist economics as a relic and accepts corporate capitalism; radical centrists favor market-based solutions.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not directly addressed; radical centrists accept markets with private corporations and do not tie acceptability to worker or public ownership. Inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Wikipedia lists Henry George among historical influences, but the Halstead and Lind tax program is a consumption tax instead, so adherents are not clearly for replacing other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Halstead and Lind propose restoring the inheritance tax, and give every child a nest egg, in line with their asset-spreading approach.

basic-income.rationale: The sources propose conditional help, jobs for those willing to work and one-time development accounts, not an unconditional income for every adult.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The manifesto supports free trade with a conscience; protective tariffs are not endorsed, though Lind personally favored economic nationalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Radical centrists favor market solutions yet endorse subsidies such as wage subsidies and government backing of energy paths, so strategic direction is split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Halstead and Lind's nest egg for every child and the manifesto's development accounts for poor children aim to spread asset ownership widely.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The manifesto accepts corporate capitalism and wage employment, with a goal of decent jobs for all who will work.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nothing suggests radical centrists want to abolish central banks; the strand favors regulated markets and fiscal responsibility. Inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages and prices are not proposed, and the sources favor market solutions; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Radical centrists criticize both major parties, back instant-runoff voting and new parties, and accept representative democracy. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; the issue is irrelevant to the sources, so neither side is inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: The manifesto accepts representative democracy and Wikipedia describes reforms to improve it, though the 'even when voters choose badly' clause is untested.

direct-votes.rationale: The reforms stress electoral process changes like instant-runoff voting rather than direct lawmaking by referendum; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: The manifesto accepts representative democracy and rejects socialist relics, which excludes councils as the basis of political power.

natural-rulers.rationale: Radical centrists seek to build majorities among ordinary people and fair opportunity, and fairness for individuals rejects rule by natural superiors.

political-violence-never.rationale: Satin came from neopacifism and the strand emphasizes civility, but the manifesto also supports armed humanitarian intervention, so the answer is inferred and not absolute.

war-builds-character.rationale: Radical centrists stress realism and ethical restraint in foreign policy, and Ethical Realism advocates modesty, not war for character.

separate-church-state.rationale: The manifesto stresses religious tolerance but proposes no policy on church and state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Radical centrism is a pragmatic secular reform program, and religion in the manifesto appears only as tolerance and shared values.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The manifesto calls for a strong supple military and public courts reforms like small claims courts, so private provision of defense and courts runs against it.

military-superiority.rationale: The manifesto wants a strong military for national security, though Ethical Realism stresses modesty, so only mild support is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The manifesto rejects balkanized racial groups and favors race-neutral fairness for individuals, which conflicts with an ethnic-based nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The manifesto rejects socialist economics as a 1960s relic and Wikipedia describes the synthesis of left and right as pragmatic, which excludes class conflict as history's driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Radical centrists support opportunity through development accounts and need-based aid and avoid outcome equality; the Halstead and Lind program centres choice.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Noel Pearson's Australian work is cited as radical centrist, but sources do not give a position on land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The manifesto prefers useful aid and fairness for individuals over guilt-driven transfers, and racial-injustice remedies are need-based; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; radical centrists favor global governance and national leadership, not civilizational blocs. Inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; the movement pairs personal responsibility with state assistance and idealism, so no direction.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The strand stresses personal responsibility alongside rights and conditional assistance, but sources do not put duties above rights; Satin endorses national service as a civic duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The manifesto lists animal rights among counter-culture gains worth keeping, suggesting some acceptance of non-instrumental value; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Radical centrists see an Information Age with large untapped opportunities and accept corporate capitalism, which is inconsistent with a disaster view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Radical centrists are optimistic but pragmatic and favor institutional reform, not accelerating disruption of institutions as an aim.

human-enhancement.rationale: The manifesto is cautiously optimistic about biotechnology, but enhancement is not addressed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses democratic reform and leadership, so handing decisions to algorithms is unlikely. Inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; adherents pair security vigilance with civil liberties, so no direction is inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Radical centrists reject nostalgia for the 1960s and look to present and future conditions, and they call for fundamental reform rather than restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Radical centrism is defined by pragmatism and realism, and borrowing from left and right whatever works, summed up as idealism without illusions.

direct-action.rationale: Radical centrists seek change through political reform, candidates, parties and electoral rules like instant-runoff voting.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; the ethos of civility and process suggests sympathy but the sources do not state it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Radical centrists embrace Information Age opportunity and corporate capitalism, so returning to foraging is outside the program.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The manifesto accepts corporate capitalism and wage work with decent jobs for all who work, which presumes a division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Goods flow through markets and conditional work-linked assistance, with need-based aid targeted at the disadvantaged rather than distribution by need as a general principle.

production-for-use.rationale: The manifesto accepts corporate capitalism, and markets are favored for social problems, so profit-based production is accepted.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The manifesto accepts corporate capitalism and rejects socialist economics as a relic, which includes the exploitation theory of profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The manifesto rejects socialist economics and revolution, accepting representative democracy. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

collective-farming.rationale: The movement accepts market institutions and rejects socialist relics, so collectivized agriculture is not on the table.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Radical centrists accept corporate capitalism and want global participation and ethical realism, rejecting the inevitability thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Radical centrists propose detailed tax reforms and fiscal responsibility, accepting taxation as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed in sources, and radical centrists combine social liberalism with personal responsibility.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Radical centrists stress fairness for individuals over group-based preferences but also want to preserve gains for women and gays as groups; no explicit stand.

conscription.rationale: The manifesto endorses universal national service as a civic duty, though conscription into the military is a narrower matter, so only mild agreement is inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Radical centrists want democratic reform and voice, with school choice as an exit-type mechanism, so voting is not subordinated; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Choice is the design criterion in Halstead and Lind's proposals, but the sources do not frame citizens as customers who can leave the state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Development accounts for poor children and guaranteed work suggest means-based freedom, though the sources do not state the philosophy.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial hereditarianism is not part of the strand, which favors race-neutral fairness and rejects balkanized groups; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Radical centrists want electoral reform such as instant-runoff voting that works through elections, not representation by families and trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: The manifesto rejects one-size-fits-all government programs and supports choices, markets and tolerance. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical centrists seek fundamental institutional reform but not a rebirth to overcome decadence; the framing is Information Age reform. Inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Radical centrist foreign policy advocates modesty and ethical realism, with global governance and aid for development.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Radical centrism is a modern democratic reform program with no feudal elements. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

bound-labor.rationale: The program is a modern democratic one centred on decent jobs for all and fairness for individuals, so bound labor is opposed. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Radical centrism prizes realism and pragmatism, which assume evidence can be weighed, rather than knowledge as power; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed beyond shared faith values like peace and grace in the manifesto.

single-common-good.rationale: Radical centrists claim to transcend left and right and find common ground, but they treat politics as solving problems with trade-offs rather than a single reasoned good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Lapid is cited as a radical centrist but that does not define the ideology.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The manifesto seeks better corporate cultures through consultants and laws, not democratic votes on running large companies; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Halstead and Lind propose government money usable at public or private schools of the family's choice, and Wikipedia lists school choice as a radical centrist reform.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Radical centrists strongly commit to fiscal responsibility and a balanced budget, even if that requires means-testing.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed directly; radical centrists favor markets but regulated for the public good, so no strong stance.

rule-by-example.rationale: Radical centrists favor concrete legal and institutional reform over reliance on rulers' moral example; inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: Humanitarian intervention is supported but UN authorization is not discussed, and radical centrists favor global governance.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Pragmatism and realism are central, but the manifesto cites shared faith values and religious tolerance, so the exclusive claim is not stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigration and welfare eligibility are not addressed in the sources.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The manifesto draws on Lawrence Mead for generous assistance conditioned on work, schooling or training.

class-collaboration.rationale: The manifesto seeks better corporate cultures and employer-employee cooperation and avoids class war framing; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nothing in the sources endorses sacrificing cultural institutions; the strand is reformist, not futurist-destructive. Inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Radical centrists support global governance and useful assistance to developing nations rather than adversarial fronts against the West; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the manifesto rejects class framing, so organizing the working class along any lines is not part of the program.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The manifesto lists women's rights among counter-culture gains worth keeping, which excludes law codifying distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Radical centrists accept corporate capitalism and market-based solutions, so banning interest is excluded.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Radical centrists favor race-neutral ideals and reject race classification even for affirmative action, so racial segregation law is opposed. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The manifesto and Halstead and Lind treat the state as an instrument to be reformed for the public, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The manifesto includes clean fossil fuels among seven paths but gives no priority to expanding oil, gas and coal.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement thesis is a conspiracy theory not found in radical centrist sources, which favor evidence-based pragmatism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Halstead and Lind propose rank-ordered voting to move beyond domination by two parties, which is a reform to widen representation though not strictly proportional. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Ethical realism advocates modesty and seeing ourselves as others see us, which rejects a special mission to spread one's government; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed, though women's rights are a counter-culture gain to keep.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Radical centrists criticize both parties and campaign for getting money out of politics and restoring civility, which implies a poor view of established politics.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is incompatible with fairness for individuals and the movement's cautious view of biotechnology.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program includes health insurance, retirement savings, development accounts and education equalization, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Radical centrists favor race-neutral ideals and racial healing, which excludes discouraging mixed marriage. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Fairness for individuals and race-neutral ideals rest on equal worth before the law, though the sources do not state it as a principle.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not applicable to radical centrism, which rejects socialism; no basis for either side.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious tolerance appears in the manifesto, so legal restriction on conversion is unlikely; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No sources link radical centrism to religion-based bans; the pragmatic reformist stance excludes it. Inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed, and the stress on school choice means religious instruction questions are left open.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Radical centrists accept representative democracy and reform to strengthen it, which presumes consent as the base of authority.

trade-surplus.rationale: The manifesto supports free trade with a conscience, not mercantilist surplus-seeking; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The manifesto supports armed humanitarian intervention and national service, which is inconsistent with an absolute rule against initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Markets and choice are favored but the movement stresses cooperation and civility, so a Social-Darwinist reading is not stated.

population-transfer.rationale: The manifesto's tolerance and fairness for individuals exclude forced removal of minorities.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; it is a philosophical formulation outside the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Radical centrists accept representative democracy and want improved government, which implies checks and balances; not stated explicitly.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement rejects socialist relics and aims to build a majority within democratic politics, not a revolutionary vanguard. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The manifesto promises decent jobs for all who work and development accounts for poor children, and prefers need-based aid, showing priority to the disadvantaged.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, though asset-spreading is a theme.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The review says Halstead and Lind offer no labor program, so no stand.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources trace poverty to institutions and policy and propose reforms, not population; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Radical centrists favor race-neutral fairness and racial healing and do not claim diversity is a problem; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Radical centrists advance electoral reforms like instant-runoff voting, not lottery selection; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Radical centrists pair security vigilance with attention to causes and civic norms, with no endorsement of suspending protections; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The market-based approach to problems implies skepticism of price fixing, though not addressed directly.

party-controls-media.rationale: Radical centrists accept representative democracy and criticize partisanship, which excludes government or party control of media. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

party-commands-army.rationale: Representative democracy and civic control of a strong supple military are assumed, with no party army. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Reforms focus on getting money out of politics rather than pay caps; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Radical centrists criticize partisan bickering and stress independents, so binding party discipline is unlikely; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Support for global governance participation and Clegg's pro-European liberal centrism suggest openness to pooled sovereignty, though not in the manifesto.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed, and the focus on institutional reform in a representative democracy suggests no strengthening of executive prerogative; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; it is outside the ideology's scope.

clerical-rule.rationale: Radical centrism accepts representative democracy and a secular reform agenda, so clerical rule is opposed. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Radical centrists support a strong military and ethical realist foreign policy, not revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Radical centrists emphasize tolerance and civil liberties and propose no censorship; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Radical centrists stress reform of institutions and civility, and nothing suggests lifting term limits; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed, though process reform is a theme.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Radical centrists support global participation and a strong military, so withdrawal from alliances is unlikely; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The movement accepts market institutions and spreads assets via accounts, not by forbidding renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: The manifesto calls for a strong supple military, not a replacement by an armed citizenry.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Radical centrists criticize politics and the left and right but sources hold no anti-educated stance; Halstead and Lind favor expertise-informed reform. Inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in sources; radical centrists mix tough-on-crime and rehabilitative strands.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Pragmatism and realism favor evidence-based curricula, while school choice allows variation; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The strand favors race-neutral ideals and civic fairness over descent-based membership; not addressed directly.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed, though the manifesto emphasizes tolerance.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; radical centrists value both civility and counter-culture gains.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The manifesto favors useful aid and trade with a conscience for developing nations but does not address debt.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed in sources, though they favor fundamental institutional reform.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Radical centrists accept representative democracy and want reform to improve it, so trading political freedoms for growth contradicts them.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The manifesto and Wikipedia support genuine assistance to developing nations, including a Marshall Plan style aid, though framed as usefulness not guilt.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed in sources, though fiscal responsibility is a theme.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Markets are regulated to serve the public good, yet property is not discussed as conditional; no direction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist state is outside radical centrism, which rejects socialist economics, so no position can be drawn from the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Satin favors market tools for energy and environmental goals, so precaution is inferred as acceptable when paired with pragmatic mechanisms.

collective-defense.rationale: The manifesto takes an internationalist, alliance-minded foreign policy; this is inferred rather than stated about mutual defense.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: A pragmatic liberal-democratic outlook is inferred to treat non-consensual annexation as illegitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Pragmatic pluralists accept religious institutions within a liberal framework; inferred from acceptance of representative democracy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A parliamentary or constitutional symbol of unity fits a consensus-seeking outlook; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Centrist pragmatists typically defend territorial integrity of democratic states; inferred, and rarely addressed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Decentralized, pragmatic federalism is consistent with the outlook; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Radical centrism accepts capitalism and representative democracy, which excludes sacred rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Need-based, pragmatic fairness is inferred to favor graduated rates over a flat tax; not stated.

character-from-environment.rationale: Reformist stress on education and opportunity implies circumstances shape people; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Representative democracy and constitutional reform imply rulers are bound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are indifferent to space as a goal, so this is a genuine split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Electoral reforms that loosen two-party dominance and checks and balances suggest a blend of institutions; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Idealism without illusions and representative democracy reject glorification of leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: A pragmatic, equality-minded reform outlook is inferred to accept shared parenting; not addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A pragmatic market-accepting outlook rejects Marxist class-struggle claims; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Accepts capitalism and property; not addressed directly, inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: A liberal-minded pragmatism favours return rights; not addressed, inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: A pragmatic, institution-focused outlook does not endorse irredentism; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Liberal democratic and pragmatic; legal punishment for apostasy conflicts with it, inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Liberal democratic values oppose clothing mandates; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split on common currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Focus on reforming existing national institutions; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Prefers common civic institutions to group-specific ones and opposes group preferences; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Civic-liberal outlook favours equal rights where people live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Pragmatic and reform-minded, stressing ideas and institutional design over a materialist theory; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Favours regulated markets with competition; inferred to back antitrust.

no-bailouts.rationale: Fiscal responsibility pulls one way, financial stability the other; adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Accepts representative democracy with checks and rejects unconstrained majorities; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Prefers need-based over race-based preferences, so parity quotas by sex run against it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Accepts regulated markets and open economies; autarky is inconsistent with it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Takes social goals from the left while keeping markets; binding standards in trade deals fit that; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Relies on market and policy incentives rather than moral exhortation; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a liberal reform outlook that treats equal rights as settled.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; the sources do not discuss natural resources or foreign control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Halstead and Lind's proposals for universal asset-building, which treat unequal starting points as a problem.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; radical centrists are pragmatic and the issue splits market-minded and global-governance-minded adherents.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The movement favours need-based rather than race-based preferences, which implies class matters more than race today.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the pragmatic, institution-minded outlook that prefers changing laws by reform to disobeying them.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on work-based social policy and market tools rather than abolishing paid work.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents differ between a leading liberal power and a balance of regional powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the borrowing of market tools from the right, which assumes prices and demand set value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Halstead and Lind's national-progressive appeal to common civic purpose and broad opportunity.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from the preference for class-based over identity-based policies.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to democratic electoral reform and regulated markets under pluralist politics.

missingStatements.text: Every citizen should be required to perform a period of national service.
missingStatements.rationale: Satin's manifesto endorses universal national service as a civic duty.

missingStatements.text: Every child should receive a publicly funded savings account to build assets by adulthood.
missingStatements.rationale: Halstead and Lind propose a nest egg at birth and the manifesto proposes development accounts for poor children.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow policy detail (child savings accounts); not worth a permanent statement every audit must answer.

missingStatements.text: Elections should use ranked-choice voting so that voters can rank candidates in order of preference.
missingStatements.rationale: Halstead and Lind propose rank-ordered voting and Wikipedia lists instant-runoff voting among radical centrist reforms.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow electoral-mechanism detail; proportional-representation partly covers electoral reform and a new statement would burden every audit.

notes: Strands differ: Lind favors immigration restriction and economic nationalism, while the Satin manifesto supports free trade with a conscience. Most statements are unaddressed in the sources, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.
